Executive structural synthesis

Italy's quarterly national-accounts picture is classified as constructive but mixed. Growth Quality: Consumption-led growth. Investment Quality: Productive-capital intensive. Competitiveness: Mixed / broadly neutral. Household Demand: Durable-led discretionary demand. External Sector: Broadly neutral external contribution. Across the five modules, 1 are favourable, 4 mixed/neutral and 0 adverse.

Investment structure & quality

The fixed-investment mix in 2026-Q2 is classified as productive-capital intensive. GFCF stood at 22.4% of GDP versus 21.5% for EU-27. Machinery/equipment plus intellectual property accounted for 46.8% of GFCF, while construction accounted for 53.1%. Total real GFCF growth was +3.3% year-on-year in 2026-Q2.

Household demand & consumption mix

The current household-demand mix is classified as durable-led discretionary demand. Real household consumption grew +1.2% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Durables accounted for 8.3% of nominal household expenditure and services for 52.3% in 2026-Q2.

Methodology and interpretation

The growth-regime, growth-balance and watchpoint labels are transparent A-CLUSTER analytical rules. They are not Eurostat classifications. The report chooses the latest quarter with headline real GDP growth and a sufficiently populated expenditure decomposition. Structural indicators such as productivity, unit labour costs and GFCF may have different release lags; their observation quarter is disclosed explicitly. The household durability module (namq_10_fcs) follows the domestic consumption concept and is not identical to the household/NPISH aggregate used in the GDP expenditure decomposition. A reconciliation residual larger than ±0.35 percentage points is flagged rather than silently treated as a complete decomposition.
Data source: Eurostat datasets namq_10_gdp, namq_10_lp_ulc, namq_10_an6 and namq_10_fcs.
